pre_conditions: [YELLOW] The rider is eligible for paratransit and, to book online, has a portal account
flow_of_events: [YELLOW] The rider signs in to the trip portal
[YELLOW] The rider selects saved home and work details
The rider requests the morning trip and the return trip in one request for the next day
The portal checks that the request arrived by 5 p.m. the day before
[YELLOW] If the request arrived after 5 p.m., then the portal holds it for dispatcher review and tells the rider it is held, not denied
[YELLOW] The portal reads the rider's chair size and lift needs from the rider profile
[YELLOW] If the chair or lift details are missing, then the portal asks the rider to enter them before continuing
[YELLOW] The portal places both trips in the trip queue for run building
[YELLOW] The portal shows the rider a confirmation that both trips were received, with each pickup window to follow once the runs are built
post_conditions: If the request arrived by 5 p.m., both trips are in the trip queue with the rider's mobility details attached
[YELLOW] If the request arrived after 5 p.m., both trips are held for dispatcher review
alternative_flows: If the rider does not book online, then reservation staff enter the same trips by phone and the flow continues from the 5 p.m. check
non_functional: [YELLOW] The portal conforms to WCAG 2.1 AA so the rider can book without staff help

uc_name: Change or Cancel Trip Same Day
pre_conditions: The rider has a booked trip for today that is assigned to a run
[YELLOW] The rider is signed in to the trip portal, unless the rider calls reservation staff
flow_of_events: The rider selects the trip and chooses a new pickup or a cancellation
The dispatch board calculates the effect on every rider and window on the run, with capacity and mobility needs
[YELLOW] The portal shows the rider what is being changed, limited to the rider's own new window and whether dispatcher approval is needed, never other riders' details
The rider submits the change and the system records who made it and when
[YELLOW] The dispatch board decides the change by its route impact
[YELLOW] If no other rider window or capacity is affected, then the board accepts the change automatically and the flow continues at the rider confirmation
[YELLOW] If another rider window or capacity is affected, then the board routes the change to the dispatcher and the portal shows the rider a pending status within 1 minute
[YELLOW] The dispatcher reviews every affected rider and window, with the overtime and deadhead effect of the change, before accepting it
[YELLOW] If the dispatcher declines the change, then the original trip stands, the driver's manifest is not changed, the portal shows the rider the reason and the flow ends
The portal shows the rider confirmation that the change was accepted
[YELLOW] If the trip was cancelled, then the board removes it from the run and releases the capacity
The dispatch board pushes the updated manifest and notes to the driver
[YELLOW] The driver acknowledges the updated manifest
[YELLOW] If the driver does not acknowledge within 2 minutes, then the board alerts the dispatcher
The notification service sends each affected rider one timely update, with no duplicates
post_conditions: The run, the driver's manifest and the rider's trip agree
The change history records what changed, who changed it and when
alternative_flows: If the rider calls instead of using the portal, then reservation staff enter the change and the flow continues at the route impact calculation
non_functional: [YELLOW] The rider sees an outcome or pending status within 1 minute of submitting
[YELLOW] Riders see no trip or mobility details belonging to other riders

pre_conditions: The rider has a trip today and the assigned van has started its run
flow_of_events: [YELLOW] The vehicle GPS reports the van's position to the system
The ETA service computes an arrival estimate from the van's position
The rider views the van's live location and arrival estimate in the portal
[YELLOW] If the rider prefers not to check the portal, then the notification service sends alerts as the van approaches
[YELLOW] The ETA service compares the estimate with the pickup window
[YELLOW] If the van is predicted to arrive outside the window, then the notification service alerts the rider once with the new estimate
The rider uses the vehicle status to decide when to go out to meet the van
post_conditions: The rider knows the van's actual status without calling dispatch
non_functional: [YELLOW] The arrival estimate is within 5 minutes of actual arrival

pre_conditions: The 5 p.m. cutoff for next-day requests has passed
flow_of_events: The dispatcher reviews the trip queue

[YELLOW] The scheduling module matches each trip to mobility needs and vehicle capacity, treating vehicle fit as a hard constraint ahead of deadhead savings and adding boarding time to each pickup from the rider's mobility needs
The dispatcher assigns runs and drivers
The dispatch board checks every run for conflicts before it reaches the driver
If a vehicle is overloaded, riders are incompatible, timing between legs is bad or a mobility detail does not match the van, then the board flags the conflict

[YELLOW] The dispatcher resolves each flagged conflict by moving a trip to another run, swapping vehicles or adjusting the shared route, and the board shows the overtime and deadhead effect of the fix
The driver receives the manifest, windows, mobility details and notes in the driver app
post_conditions: Every run for the next day is free of flagged conflicts and assigned to a driver and vehicle
non_functional: Capacity, mobility needs and pickup windows are visible together on one board

uc_name: Add Trip After Runs Are Built
pre_conditions: Runs for the day have been built
A trip must be added, such as a power-chair trip
flow_of_events: Reservation staff enter the added trip
The dispatch board flags any capacity conflict on the shared run
The dispatcher reviews the effect on all downstream pickups
The dispatcher resequences the manifests and moves an affected rider if needed
If a vehicle swap is needed, then the dispatcher swaps vehicles on the run
The dispatch board pushes the updated manifest and notes to each affected driver
The board records what was changed, who changed it and when
post_conditions: The added trip is on a run with no capacity conflict
The affected pickups stay within their windows
non_functional: Updated manifests reach drivers without the dispatcher phoning them

pre_conditions: The driver has the current manifest with pickup location, mobility details and notes
flow_of_events: The driver arrives at the correct pickup location within the pickup window
[YELLOW] The driver confirms the vehicle can accommodate the rider's chair
[YELLOW] If the assigned vehicle cannot accommodate the chair, then the dispatcher swaps vehicles
The driver gives the rider enough space and time to deploy the ramp and board without being rushed
If the rider's attendant is present, then the attendant boards at no charge under program rules
The driver takes the rider to the destination
The driver records road notes in the system instead of by radio
[YELLOW] The driver records the trip as completed in the driver app
post_conditions: The rider is delivered and the trip is recorded as completed
[YELLOW] On a return trip, the rider is home before the attendant's evening visit
non_functional: The rider boards safely without being rushed

pre_conditions: The dispatcher has started a shift and the day's runs are on the board
flow_of_events: The dispatcher checks the day's runs, vehicle assignments and driver notes
The board shows pickups and drop-offs as they move along
The board shows any driver held up on the previous leg
If there are late pull-outs, stacked exceptions, a driver falling behind or too many same-day changes, then the board shows an early warning
The dispatcher balances the routes
The dispatcher hands the board to the next dispatcher at shift end
post_conditions: The next dispatcher has an accurate board
non_functional: The board stays accurate throughout the shift

pre_conditions: [YELLOW] No-show and late-cancel events are recorded per rider
flow_of_events: The dispatcher opens the view of repeated no-shows and late cancels
The board shows patterns across riders and trips
[YELLOW] The dispatcher uses the patterns when planning runs to reduce capacity lost to no-shows
post_conditions: Repeat patterns are known to dispatch instead of being treated as one-off surprises

pre_conditions: A contractor invoice has been received
Dispatch records for the billing period are linked to completed trips
flow_of_events: The budget manager reviews the invoice against dispatch records
If billed hours differ from completed service, then the reporting module flags an invoice exception
The budget manager requires a correction from the contractor for each exception
[YELLOW] The contractor resubmits the corrected invoice
non_functional: [YELLOW] Trip cost data matches completed service

pre_conditions: Reservations, dispatch events, completed trips, cancellations and no-shows are linked per trip
flow_of_events: The reporting module provides scheduled versus actual revenue hours, deadhead mileage, vehicle utilization and overtime attribution
The budget manager compares actual trip volumes against the adopted budget
[YELLOW] The reporting module reports on-time performance separately for return trips
The budget manager reviews cost per passenger trip, overtime and contractor invoice variance

If costs run above plan, then the budget manager revises the forecast, defers nonessential administrative spending and works with scheduling staff on earlier schedule review, without cutting eligible trips
[YELLOW] The reporting module produces federal reports from the linked trip records
The budget manager weighs service changes against their effect on riders, vehicle utilization, overtime and federal obligations
post_conditions: The variance analysis is complete without manual reconciliation
non_functional: Cost-allocation data is reliable at the trip level
